reviews.text: Love that they open late and that on Friday, Saturday and Sunday they are open 24 hours. We have been having nothing but good experience with them, they saved our dog life. They have been very good to her, and very nice to us. It is pricey but I understand why. I definitely recommend this place.

On July 1, 2026, my dog was euthanized at Angel of Mercy Critical Care, and communal cremation was initially arranged. On July 2, at approximately 6 p.m., I called the practice to change the cremation arrangement from communal to private. Staff confirmed that the change had been made. I was quoted approximately two weeks for the return of her ashes.
After that period passed without an update, I left several voicemails and spoke with front-desk staff, but I did not receive information about the status of her ashes. The practice directed me to contact its third-party cremation provider. When I contacted that provider, I was told it could not locate a record for my dog.
On October 2, while visiting the practice for another appointment, I again requested an update. Staff could not locate the ashes and suggested that weather might be affecting the delay. By that point, three months had passed since my request for private cremation.
I requested a refund. The practice offered to refund $100 for the private-cremation charge. I also requested a refund of the remaining amount I paid for cremation because I had not received the ashes or a clear explanation of what happened.
On October 6, a manager called from a blocked number and left a voicemail asking me to return the call. Because the number was blocked, I could not call the manager back directly. The only callback number provided was the office number, and the office was closed at the time. I called that number and left a message. As of October 7, I had not received a response.
To resolve this complaint, I am requesting a refund of the full amount paid for cremation services and a written explanation of what happened to my dog’s remains, including whether a private cremation occurred and whether her ashes can still be returned.
This has been heartbreaking. Beyond the delay, the repeated difficulty obtaining basic information has made an already painful loss more distressing

My Fur baby passed away while I was on vacation. The hospital held him for seventy two hours until I could get back. I'm very appreciative of that service and  with the respect and compassion in which they treat their clients.

They let me dog pass alone didn't call and give me a chance to say good bye. Just said we called to get Payment for cpr we preformed. After telling me she was doing good and I could pick her up soon. They don't help. They don't answer questions, they make promises they can't keep. Don't take your pets here.
Great service, very nice people

If I could give this place a -100 rating, I absolutely would.

I called at 10:00 p.m. specifically to ask if they were still accepting walk-ins. The receptionist told me yes, so I drove 35 minutes with my dog, only to arrive and be told they would not see him.

What makes this even more frustrating is that there was only one other patient there. If they were no longer accepting walk-ins, that should have been communicated to me over the phone. I would have completely avoided wasting 35 minutes driving there, only to be turned away at the door.

This was extremely unprofessional, inconsiderate, and completely unacceptable. When someone is calling for veterinary care, they are trusting your staff to provide accurate information—especially when they are making a 35-minute trip with their pet.

A simple, accurate answer over the phone would have prevented this entire situation. I will not be returning, and based on this experience, I would strongly encourage others to think twice before relying on this establishment for their pet’s care.
When I got there the first thing they said was there is a 3 hour wait.so I left because my Cat was crying and crying.

My daughter took her kitten because she was concerned about how it was acting and its lack of wanting to eat. Thankfully it was open as it was later at night around 9 pm. They told her the kitten has low body temp and low blood sugar. Mind you we found this kitten outside so we were not sure its age but just knew it was extremely young, being bottle fed and thought it might have just picked up an infection. They gave her medication for its blood sugar put it in an incubator for a little and said everything else looked good and sent her on her way. Im giving it a one star review because when she left the kitten stopped breathing. She called them to let them know and how she was on her way back to have them look at it. They told her that they were about to close and to look for another location. By the time they found one the kitten died. I am so disappointed in the fact that they turned her away. I understand business hours but they had just seen her, evaluated the kitten said it was all ok and when she needed them again they told her to go elsewhere. I feel like the time they spent looking for a place was the difference between life and death for the kitten.

Her words to me were that they were going to have to "cut off his head and send it off"

I wasn't originally going to leave a review. I was devastated, angry, and honestly just wanted to take my kitten home and grieve.

I brought Ollie in extremely sick. He was weak, struggling, and could barely hold his head up. I was crying and terrified, but I was willing to spend upwards of the quoted $2,000+ if there was a reasonable chance they could save him.

While Ollie was being treated and given an IV, a vet tech was bitten by him. I was shocked when I was told this because of how incredibly weak he was. I was told he had somehow mustered enough energy to bite her.

Eventually, I had to make the heartbreaking decision to euthanize him.

Then the vet tech came back and told me we had another problem. Because Ollie had bitten her, he would have to be tested for rabies.

Her words to me were that they were going to have to "cut off his head and send it off."

Those were the words used while I was actively grieving the realization that I would lose him very soon.

I understand now that rabies testing can require brain tissue. That doesn't change what it was like to hear those words at that moment. I was already trying to process that my kitten was dying, and suddenly I was being told that after euthanasia, his head was going to be cut off and sent away.

There were also additional charges being discussed as a result of everything that followed. To the veterinarian's credit, he was compassionate enough to remove the holding fee, and I appreciated him for doing that.

I ultimately paid and left. I wasn't even going to write a review.

Then I went back today to pick up Ollie.

I have his body now, and I can't even bring myself to unwrap him because I have to face what was done to his body after he died. I have to accept that the little kitten I brought there hoping they could save is not coming home to me the way I brought him in.

And while picking him up, there is now a warning posted (that wasn't there before) about aggressive behavior and profane language not being tolerated. After what I experienced there, seeing it felt like a slap in the face.

So yes, I used profanity.
Excuse me for being devastated that day, learning I couldn't bring his body back in one piece. Excuse me for assuming a veterinary  hospital would use proper measures when using a needle while handling an animal.

To hear his head would have to be "cut off" and sent away. Was not even a thought that day.

And now I have to sit here with his wrapped body knowing that before I can see him again, I have to confront that reality.

If a veterinary clinic wants grieving pet owners to control every word that comes out of their mouths during one of the most traumatic moments of their lives, then compassion needs to go both ways.

COMPASSION NEEDS TO GO BOTH WAYS.

I didn't threaten anyone. I didn't hurt anyone. I was devastated, angry, crying, and yes, I cussed.

There is a difference between abusive behavior and a grieving pet owner saying the f word after being told her kitten's head has to be cut off.

I sincerely hope nobody else ever has to experience what I did.
I brought Ollie there hoping to save his life.

Today I brought home what was left of him.
And I still can't bring myself to unwrap him.
Glad they are here to help our senior pup.

The front desk Lady was inconsiderate to my friend who brought in her cat who had died by 2 dog attack. The cat was completely dismembered and the front desk lady is asking how much the cat weighs and what color he was. She had no sympathy what so ever. Never even said “sorry for your loss”. For a vet hospital, the one that answers the phones and runs the front desk needs to have sympathy and compassion! Do better!

Angel of Mercy was there for us during an incredibly difficult time with our dog. She has been dealing with cancer and significant pain, and the team helped us get her pain under control and made her much more comfortable.

Everyone we interacted with genuinely cared about both our dog and our family. When you’re watching your pet struggle, having a veterinary team that listens and focuses on keeping them comfortable means so much.

Had to take my kitty here as they were the only vet open on Saturday's. My cat has normally been good with vets before this, but he was acting out on this visit. Which I understand is difficult for the staff to control. The techs and the doctor seemed to place most of the blame on me. Telling me I should've given my cat gabapentin before I brought him in. I've never had a bad vet experience with my cat before this, so I didn't think I would need to have gabapentin. They had none of the tools that would help with a scared and sick cat, like a EZ-Nabber or even cat proof gloves.
They expected me to subdue my scared and sick cat myself as they watched from the corner. If they had the proper tools to help us, this wouldn't have been such a traumatic vet visit. The staff knew he was scared and still insisted on giving him a 150 dollar long lasting antibiotic shot, even when I told them he was calm at home and I could give him pills. It was after a 10 minute long session of basically torturing my cat to stay still so they could give him two shots, they admitted the antibiotic shot wouldn't be possible to administer. They then said they would refund the 150 dollars for the shot, and send us home with 20 dollars worth of antibiotic pills. I found this confusing, why would you insist on traumatizing my cat when there was an easier and cheaper option.... I understand that scared cats are hard to manage, but this is a vet? They should've acted in a more professional manner and had the tools to take care of a scared cat. My cat definitely wasn't the first scared cat to go through their doors. They were able to help my kitty, but it was not a good experience. Do better.

If youre in a hurry or on a time crunch this isnt the place for you. But they actually care about our furry family members and pay attention to all the details and explore every option to make sure that your pet gets the precisely correct diagnosis and treatment. 24hours so they handle any emergency that comes up. Really great people in the right positions to do what they do.

The level of care depends on how deep your pockets are. $100 just for the vet to walk in the room. Any testing and or meds make the costs just go up up up! Our city has terrible resources for poor people who love their pets on a Sunday morning
Friendly service and always helpful!

Took our beloved Dotson last night and waited 2 hours and never called. They made my son wait outside because she could be contagious but everyone else was inside. He left because he felt they forgot about him. Our dog is fully vaccinated and he had shot records. He left at 11:30 am came home at 2 am and was never seen. This morning our fur baby is eating and running around feeling better. I will never go here again

Y’all are disgusting people the way yall treated my sister and BIL before she had to put down her fur baby was horrible I WILL be running my mouth about yall around Texas, she wasn’t just a stray she was family I hope the worst for yalls business
Michelle and Dr. Were great. Lucky is home recovering.

I took my cat, Nala, to Angel of Mercy when she was refusing to eat, drink or use her litter box and just wasn't acting like herself. Alli was extremely compassionate and sweet with my cat and treated her like one of her own animals both times she saw my cat. Dr. Perkins as well made both of our visits extremely quick and easy and gave me all the information, including a quote,  I needed to get my cat transferred over to another clinic for her surgery as soon as possible. Thank you both for your help and your compassion with my baby, she's now home and in recovery.

At first I would say this vet was great, my doctor was wonderful and attentive. This is a cheaper ER vet (ER fee) so that is a plus, emergency visits are always going to be expensive but compared to others, this is a good cheaper option.

Now with my complaints, after having a culture sent out for my cat which alone was about 300$, I received no call. I had to call back 10 days later for them to then say that they did receive it and a doctor would call me the next day to explain. This never happened so I went elsewhere for help because my cat was peeing blood. This morning, a month later, I receive a call stating they were sorry and no one told them that the culture was back and that they could explain the results to me if I called back. I was also told my cats sodium levels were extremely high, the new vet I went to said they were normal and this was likely a machine error. Honestly, very disappointed that I wasted my money for this. If you need a cheap option, this might be okay for you. But if you are okay spending a little more to go somewhere else where they will actually get back to you about lab work, go somewhere else. Hopefully I can get a refund due negligence of proper care and procedure.

I came here on April 6 following weeks of horrible vet visits at other places. My dog had jaundice and was very ill and we couldn’t figure out why. This vet gave my dog so much care and medicine for an affordable price. They saw us immediately and were so helpful to us.

We had gone to multiple other vets that week and none of them gave us any option of medication or care, instead they just wanted to euthanize my dog and charge us $1000’s. They wouldn’t even give her medicine for pain or nausea to make her comfortable. They weren’t interested in finding the cause and they all told us it was “probably” cancer or terminal (even though they never did biopsies/ x rays). Every other vet said my dog was gonna die, but the vets here saw hope and 3 months later my dog is still alive and the best she’s ever been.

The Angel of mercy vet said it could have been an infection and they were right, they gave us antibiotics and some liver support meds and it healed her. They actually wanted my dog to be okay and to live, which apparently isn’t common at a vet.

Angel of mercy didn’t jump to conclusions or make us feel stupid and hopeless. They were so nice and quick to help. They gave my dog nausea meds immediately which I had been begging for at other places. I will only ever come here. I don’t remember the names of the people who helped us but THANK YOU for everything!!! 100 stars

I would like to say that there is one person here, Ross, that was so awesome and attentive and understanding. He was a front office staff.

However, the rest of my experience here was a nightmare. My daughter’s service dog was bleeding profusely following a surgery one week earlier at another facility. The front staff showed no sense of urgency and did bare minimum to do anything. Sat and waited so long that we almost loaded her up and brought her somewhere else. They came out to the car and said they’d see her. They took her back and did the initial exam. They came back and said they needed to do exploratory surgery and quoted $2700.

All the while her dog is laying their bleeding. Continuously asked about payment, which I understand, but completely uncaring about the cost and the stress it caused. (Side note being that my daughter is 8 months pregnant and did not need all the extra stress).

They gave vague information about what they were doing and what was happening. Got the money together and they did the surgery. No active bleeding but said there was tissue and stuff on the bladder. Stated if they tried to remove it, it was a good chance that she wouldn’t pee without assistance. So they left it as is.

The next day they monitored for active bleeding. Everything was fine and called a few hours before pick up saying she wasn’t really going potty. They wanted to sedate her and do a catheter. With the bladder issue previously being brought up, why wasn’t this done during surgery or something?

They told her dad to request $4500 when he applied for care credit. They knew how much they were charging prior to any services being started. Seeing as the final bill was almost $4000.

Also, prior to pick up, they advised my daughter that if she did not pay in full at the time of pickup, they would put her dog down. What kind of cruel bs are you spewing?!? Why would you say that to her??? Why would you threaten her with that? She just spent almost 4 grand and you don’t think she’d pay what was left? Y’all are sick and I’ll make sure everyone I know knows it. Shame on you.

It’s a 24 HOUR VET CLINIC that is closed in the middle of the day, right as we bring our dog to get checked on. This is one of the cheaper places near us and it would be insanely helpful to not have to drive over to a CLOSED STORE in the middle of a working weekday, in the middle of the day. Maybe 24 Hour service is not y’all’s strong suit.

My Husband Brought a male cat named LEO to the clinic on Sunday, we had noticed that he was not acting the same, so we thought it best to take him. The 2 Dr's were very compassionate and caring. You could see they were knowledgeable and caring. Dr. Perkins & Dr. Dhakal. Although at checkout 2,700.00 later the receptionist specifically told my husband that we might have to take him back to another vet since y'all are only open until 8 am, that she would make sure that my Husband got every record needed to show the people at Thrive where they recommended we take him including his x-rays which we PAID for. This poor cat was still not breathing well, so my husband took him to Thrive as suggested, but when he went to find the files that the Dr. at Thrive needed were not sent. They wanted us to pay another 900.00 to 1200.00 for a CT scan ( if we would have had the information which we paid for and were assured that we would get)  So I called Angel of Mercy clinic around 11am while we were still trying to save this poor guy, and left a very DETAILED message about not reciving the xrays, and the Dr @ Thrive said they didnt even put what size needle used to extract the mucas from his chest.  I received a text message saying that  I could text that number back, which I did with no answer at all. The Dr. at Thrive tried to also reach out to get the " correct" medical information that was needed, again... No answer or common  curtesy at all. * Do NOT set up a text message to tell folks to text you at that number, and not have anyone monitoring it. When your office opened the next day at 4 we called to ask why the images and correct information was not sent, and the girl just wanted to argue with my Husband. She kept interrupting him and saying that she sent them. Or Why the HELL would I have called looking for the xrays along with the dr. from thrive. Girlfriend. My Husband has a damn Masters degree and is a program manager at our local base. Do you really think that he wouldn't be able to open  it. They sent the same email twice. we asked to speak with a manager ( Leslie) again.... NO call nada. Today is now Tuesday and we just called  ALEX to see if " Leslie" was available and this dude literally said that " She is very busy" hmmm But we are not? 3k later and we don't even have the correct information. We never received his x-rays in time.... We will NEVER use this place again. If you really cant even send x-rays? you need a new job. Thanks to the Dr's though. this has nothing to do with you both were great. Your staff defiantly needs training on how to use a computer. Its horrible when you bring a beloved pet who is so sick, and then we do all we are supposed to, but y'all can ignore us for 3 days. I have never been so disgusted and disappointed in customer service. I would highly recommend folks taking their beloved babies to THRIVE over Angle of Mercy. Laura & Jose Bonillas and LEO
Thank you soooo much!!

I always hate having to come here (simply bc it means I have an emergency with one of my fur babies) but they are always fantastic. My dog was sprayed in the eyes by a skunk and they were starting to swell. I was seen by a tech quickly (they had us wait out in the car due to the smell) and she showed me how to flush my dog’s eyes. The tech was so nice and gave tips for how to get rid of the smell and my dog is doing so much better now.

I took my dog in for bloody stools and bloody vomiting after I changed her food. They upsell you on every single thing even though your pet doesn’t need 1/2 of the stuff they’re pushing and when you tell them no they just ignore you and charge you anyways. I ended up spending close to 1,000.00 because they gave me several meds that do the same thing for my dog. Won’t be going back.

I was so disappointed with the lack of compassion to my pet.  My husband took our Golden in at 7 am with no food in her belly,  at 5pm they had still not even started surgery.  What was supposed to be a simple spayed procedure never got done.  My husband spoke with the doctor when he dropped her off and the doctor/owner said he would be able to get right on her.  It was postponed all day and we were never notified of the delay.  Our heart dropped when we learned she had been caged with no food or water all day.  We will never return.
Excellent urgent pet care facility!! Friendly, professional, kind, all the things you want when your fur baby isn't feeling well.
Fast and friendly and good.

I want to thank The Veterinarian and staff last night who saved my dog Meaty’s life. After a long family event we came home to our dog in distress, we quickly googled a facility that was open and this was the second place I called. When I tell you god is good, he is amazing. My husband drove us here super quick, while I prayed for our dog to make it. The staff were quick on getting Meaty the proper treatment. They saved his life. Good facilities no longer exist it’s always about the money. But if you want a Vet that genuinely cares Angel of Mercy is the place.

I'll never forget what ya'll did my three month old puppy. You basically tortured her. We'll guess what? She's almost 14 years old now. No thanks to you. You know what you did. I can't believe you're still in business after ripping us off for over $2000

I've been twice. The first time, life-saving! The second time, life-changing. Both times, filled with compassion and understanding. This is an emergency veterinarian hospital so it obviously is going to be a bit more expensive than your regular everyday veterinarian. But, in an emergency situation, this is definitely the place to go and bring your fur baby.

My cat was having a medical emergency last night and we rushed him here for care. We couldn’t get inside right away and waited a while before someone would buzz us in. The girl at the front desk asked what was going on and I explained the situation all just for her to tell me that they weren’t accepting anymore pets tonight. Completely wasted our time! If you aren’t accepting any pets put a sign on your door! It’s an urgent care so they should know that every minute counts. I would recommend CityVet for anyone needing care for their pets. The staff and doctor are amazing. They saw us right away, they had so much compassion and they saved my cat. I will only be taking my cats and other pets to CityVet going forward.

The med they gave my dog made her sicker. Not trustworthy, not helpful, long wait time, super overpriced. The staff helping me were attentive and supportive, that was the only positive part of the visit. The rest not great at all. Do not recommend, be cautious.

I had a really disappointing experience at this emergency vet. When you bring your pet in during an emergency, you expect urgency, compassion, and clear communication but that’s not what we received. The staff seemed disorganized and inattentive, and we were left waiting far longer than what felt reasonable given the situation.

I also felt pressured into making expensive decisions out of fear. The situation was presented as much more serious than it actually turned out to be, and I was strongly encouraged to leave my dog overnight, which ended up costing around $1,900. After all of that, I was told she had a rectal prolapse—which needs treatment, but is not the kind of immediately fatal emergency it was made out to be. That felt incredibly misleading and upsetting.

To make matters worse, when I picked up my dog, she was clearly distressed—panting heavily and shaking. Her harness and collar reeked of urine,It did not feel like she was kept comfortable or properly cared for during her stay. Use them at your own risk.

Do not come here for an emergency! Not only is it old and nasty it is the most expensive vet hospital I’ve ever been too. My dog was diagnosed with pyometra  and needed an emergency surgery. The vet and technician did not seem to be confident, they made jokes and did not take us seriously. I truly believe they do not care about your animals they only want your money. They quoted me $4000 and I’m currently getting surgery done elsewhere for $1800 at a way better facility!

Took our little 15 yr old pup in for a bite in the neck from an attack from another dog. Our pup look a little alert but we knew he was in pain and was bleeding from neck. After taking him in, Karla, front desk/tech was very compassionate and helpful to us and our pup. After Dr Perkins evaluated our pup, we were told that he would have to be sedated and have X-rays done ($509) later, comes and tells us he has a punctured windpipe and would need emergency surgery. After asking how much that would cost, said could be $5k, $8k, could run to $13k or he would have to be put down. And if they kept him overnight there, he would be put on IV and meds. We asked if he could be sent home with antibiotics, she said no. After realizing how old our pup was we decided we figured if he was going to die, we wanted him to die at home. We brought him home, gave him his pain meds and gave him chicken broth and water for two days and we took turns watching him sleep. Long story short, cared for him at home, little by little he got his appetite and strength and is walking and looks normal. No surgery. Just thank God he is still here with us. But thanks to Karla who texted the following days after to check on him. She was the best and compassionate with our Gizmo!
Be very wary of these critical care facilities unless you have lots of money for nothing.
Great and informative staff!!!

Our family brought our dog Roger to this clinic during an emergency. He was extremely sick and we were already going through one of the most painful moments a family can experience.
What made the situation even worse was the complete lack of empathy from the staff.
While we were crying and trying to process that our dog was dying, the only thing we kept hearing from the front desk was pressure about payment. Over and over again we were told to pay immediately. At one point I had to step outside because I was crying so much, and even then the focus remained on payment instead of showing even the smallest amount of compassion.
Let me be clear: we were never refusing to pay. My husband was inside preparing to pay and handle everything. That was never the issue. The issue was the cold and insensitive way we were treated while our dog was suffering and our family was grieving.
Before our dog was even properly sedated to relieve his pain, the repeated focus was on payment rather than care or empathy. In a moment where families are emotionally devastated, basic humanity should come first.
We understand that veterinary care costs money. That is not the problem. The problem is the complete absence of compassion during one of the hardest moments of our lives.
Because of this experience, I cannot recommend this clinic to anyone. When people bring their pets to an emergency hospital, they deserve medical care but also dignity, patience, and empathy. Unfortunately, we experienced none of that here.

I would not recommend this animal critical care clinic based on my experience on March 7, 2027. While my dog was actively dying, the front desk staff repeatedly asked us to make payments and showed no compassion or empathy during an extremely difficult moment. The interaction felt cold and insensitive when basic kindness and understanding were needed the most.

This also does not appear to be an isolated issue, as there are other reviews mentioning similar experiences with the clinic’s front desk and their lack of compassion. No pet owner should have to deal with repeated payment requests and rude behavior while saying goodbye to their pet.

I hope the clinic reviews how their staff communicates with families during emergencies and end-of-life situations and improves the level of empathy shown to people facing the loss of their pets.
Staff didn’t waste anytime helping my kitty when we rushed in! Saved his safe! Much love and blessings.
Alex always provides the best services, friendly & kind. Goes 10/10

Great staff! I'm so happy they were open when we needed emergency care for our tuxedo cat. They were caring and kept me apprised of everything they were doing. They were able to address his fever and abscessed wound! It's not pretty, but they placed a shunt for drainage and he was feeling better within 12 hours!

My cat Gizmo had been sick for about a week. He was very lethargic, threw up once and was not his regular energetic self.  I called and was told I could be a walk in and the visit would be $109.00.

Gizmo was seen quickly by the Tech who went over the list of recommended services.  Gizmo used to chew on plastic so I was concerned with a possible blockage.  The Tech recommended (after discussing with the Veterinarian) that I have a bloodwork done.  The bloodwork cost $299.27 on top of the visit charge of $109.00.  He also recommended an anti nausea shot so my cat wouldn’t throw up anymore.  That shot was $96.05.  The bloodwork stated my cat had elevated RBC, hematocrit, hemoglobin, rdw, wbc, neutrophils, monocytes, glucose which after a google search means dehydrated.  The next recommendation was a series of X-rays for possible blockage, glucose test to see if my cat was diabetic, fluids, a warming pad ($18.20) since my cat had a low temp. The quoted total was over $2500.00.  I told the tech, I can’t afford that. So he said how about the fluids ($55.00)  and an antibiotic ($34.42)?  He also mentioned my cat had pee’d on himself (which he hadn’t done until then).  Needless to say $586.80 later, I left with my cat and went home.  He died two days later and I still don’t know why.

I would not recommend this facility unless you have money or are approved for Care Credit.  It appears the Angel of Mercy was off on Friday, when I had my visit.
Very knowledgeable and helpful. Great place to take your pet. Work pmt. Plans too. Thanks.

My dog started having seizures, so I rushed him to the vet early in the morning. Thankfully, they brought him back right away! It turned out he was having strokes. The care was incredibly quick, and everyone was so attentive. They were so nice and patient with me, who was so distraught, and gave me and my wife space to be with our teddy bear for the last time. We would love to thank everyone there for how they treated us and my fur baby.
Great people and care. Had to wait a bit so more critical patients could he taken care of but thats totally understandable. They treat you great here

Thank you so much to the staff for taking care of our sweet corgi who had to stitches on her ear at 12am at night. They took her right back while paper work was being filled out. They were very clear and kind about what they were doing. Our dog had to stay the night for observation and they took great care of her. 24hr vet does come with it’s price but our girl is worth everything and our care was worth every penny.

Front desk was very nice & took our info. There was a very short wait time. When our cat was seen they were very patient and informative and answered all our questions. Helped us understand everything very well. They were honest and reasonable with their recommendations.

I want to give a very special thank you to Karla for the exceptional compassion and care she showed while taking care of my dog. During a very stressful time, Karla took the time to truly listen to all of my concerns, answered my questions with patience, and made sure I felt heard and supported every step of the way. Her kindness, empathy, and genuine care made such a difference and brought me a lot of comfort.

I also appreciate Dr. Dhakal for his professionalism and for providing great care to my dog. Overall, the experience was made so much better because of Karla’s compassion and attentiveness. I am incredibly grateful for everything they did for us.

Last month took my cat to this vet and spent over thousands for treatment. And they made a mistake in my cats record and insurance won’t cover the bill. Asked the vet for help and didn’t corporate at all. To future customer make sure everything in your cats medical record is correct.

Our dog went into cardiac arrest on a Sunday morning and passed before we could get to Angel of Mercy. They were super when we arrived, bringing a gurney to the car and then allowing us to have a room with our dog to wait for our daughters to arrive and say goodbye (we had the room nearly 45 minutes). Excellent customer service! Thank you for your kindness.

Took care of my baby Thor
Very nice people. Very caring

Angel of Mercy has always shown extraordinary compassion to every animal (my own pets and homeless dogs and cats) I've taken to them. These people actually are terrible with no heart or soul brought my cat in and they charged me 100$ to look at him and then told me he had hypothermia and treatment would be 2 thousand up front no other options no help offered no payment plans my cat died 3 hours later because of these greedy no good supposed “life savers”

The vet knew how sick my Elsa was and not once did he ever tell me that I should have her humanly euthanized… he saw the yellow to her skin.. after a few days of crying and being absolutely miserable about the fact that I paid 450$ just for her to come home and die. I talked to a few other vets and they said that looking at videos is Elsa and pics that they should have mentioned that it would be best to humanely euthanize her of course it’s not what I wanted but if it’s best for Elsa and what needed to be done so she didn’t suffer I would have just came and had that done. This cat was my everything and I’ll never forgive myself for this mistake but I was high off emotions and no sleep for two days. The vet is the professional and doctor not me of course I’m gonna try to save her but I know it was her oancreas and he even mentioned that so why would he not tell me that euthanizing her as sick as she was would be what’s best I paid the 150$ for him to look at her for 1 minute… he knew. The vet tech was very nice and the doctor was not rude or mean but when he knows an animal is that sick he should be honest with the customer and tell them that euthanizing would be best if the situation calls for it and mine sure did sadly. Now I don’t have money to cremate her because I spent the 450$ I had giving her iv fluid. The medicine is useless I didn’t even open it bc she died soon as I got home. I wish I could return it but the medicine wasn’t even expensive it was the ug for four hours that cost 450 plus the 150$ co pay . Please consider being more upfront with your patient so the animal doesn’t suffer. It’s not about the money the money is gone… yall have the money it’s about that out of that almost 500$ she still suffered. Vet care is just outrageous these days it’s honestly sickening to me how much vets charge.. yet non profits charge way less their just always so busy and hard to book with vets know we love our babies and will do anything for them. I just hope Elsa forgives me for this. Please learn from my mistake and ask if euthanizing should be the option since the vet doesn’t bring it up at all if your baby is very sick like mine we aren’t thinking straight when we are dealing with a very sick fur baby so please consider being upfront with the patient . I know I won’t get a refund but I just hope he knows that he should have offered and mentioned euthanizing her how bad sick she was and how yellow she was I’m not the doctor…
I brought my cat with an eye injury. The staff and doctor were great.  Fortunately it was not as serious as we initially thought, but the care we got was great.

I want to thank the staff for their help always. My dog was attacked by a pit bull and his lower mandible was severely damaged. I cannot say enough wonderful things about this emergency vet clinic. My sweet Elvis was attacked by two huskies and needed emergency care—he required sedation, stitches, X-rays, an IV, and pain medicine. The entire staff moved quickly, and the moment they saw me crying in the parking lot carrying him, they immediately rushed to help and got him back right away. Their compassion and professionalism in such a scary moment meant the world to me.

Dr. Dhakal was amazing—thorough, calm, and so dedicated in making sure Elvis got the best possible care. I am forever grateful for how carefully and quickly he treated him.

But I want to give a very special thank you to Xander at the front desk. He saw me at one of the worst, most emotional moments of my life, and he stayed with me until I could calm down. He offered comfort, reassurance, and even managed to make me laugh through my tears and fear. That kind of kindness and genuine care can’t be taught—it made all the difference while I waited for updates on Elvis.

I will always remember the compassion this clinic showed, and I will forever be grateful to Dr. Dhakal and especially to Xander for being such a bright light in a very dark moment. Thank you from the bottom of my heart.

I spoke to the front desk person a little over a month ago to inquire about getting a kitten spayed. I had heard they may be a more affordable option to have a spay done, so I asked if she could give me an estimate over the phone. The lady on the phone said the process was to bring in the kitten early on a Friday and they would do an exam on kitten to ensure they were healthy to do the spay and provide an estimate.  She also said that the initial exam for the kitten would be free.  And that if I wanted to do the spay the day of the exam, I could.  Fast forward to today when I brought in my kitten.  I explained that I wanted to have her spayed.  They requested I call her regular vet so they could verify she was up to date on her vaccinations. I got them on the phone and her regular vet confirmed.  My kitten was then taken to the back for an exam by the vet.  She was brought back to the room and shortly after came back in with a paper that had the estimate of $1178 - $1348.   I explained it was not going to make sense for me to move forward with the spay because her regular vet quoted me $300-$400 for the spay.  She said she understood and I proceeded to go checkout with the front desk.  They said I would need to pay $75 for today.  I questioned why I needed to pay the $75 but the gentleman told me it was because it was for a consultation.  I am frustrated for multiple reasons.  For one, it is not hard to provide a general estimate over the phone.  Secondly, I don't mind paying for services rendered.  However, my kitten is healthy and I didnt need to bring her in for someone to tell me that...but additionally I was advised over the phone that there would be not be any kind of fee for her the day I brought her in when they described what the process was for me to have her spayed- other than the spay itself.  Makes perfect sense.  That is not what happened today and it honestly feels like such a scam.  Highly disappointed.  Needless to say, my kitten is now scheduled to see her regular vet for a spay next week at Hooves and Paws in Helotes (highly recommend by the way).  My time and $75 could have been spent elsewhere had they been up front with me when I first called them over a month ago to inquire about the spay. I had another one of my kittens in not too long ago and was very pleased with my visit- so today was extremely surprising but left a horrible taste in my mouth.

WOULD NOT RECOMMEND. This place is telling people a consultation for a kitten being spayed is FREE , the initial consultation. My mother went in because again why not they said it was FREE to go through the process to receive the final estimate to get her kitten spayed. They gave her an estimate of $1,400 when our original vet charges under $500….. THEN CHARGED MY MOTHER $75 for the FREE CONSULTATION. she had forgotten they said it was free BUT the dr was on the phone in front of her telling another person the same thing that it was FREE. So she said OH! Right! It’s free so what is this $75 I just paid. And they just gave her a BS answer because she had already paid. Thank you for scamming my mother. 👍 stop telling people the initial consultation is FREE.

I recently visited Angel of Mercy Animal Critical Care with high hopes for quality care, but unfortunately, my experience was far from satisfactory. We were attended by Dr. Arynne Robinson, and I left feeling disappointed and frustrated.
Firstly, despite arriving before other families, we waited for hours without receiving any treatment for our dog. This long wait was compounded by the lack of communication and updates from the staff.
When we finally saw the veterinarian, we were shocked by the accusation that our dog had been given marijuana, which was completely unfounded. This assumption overshadowed the actual medical needs of our pet.
Moreover, after paying $400, we received no substantial treatment or relief for our dog. Despite being told she needed an IV for fluids, there seemed to be a rush to discharge us without addressing this need.
Overall, the experience was distressing and unsatisfactory. I hope that Angel of Mercy Animal Critical Care can improve their service and communication in the future to better serve their patients and their families.

I'm writing this letter with a heavy heart, consumed by disappointment and frustration with Angel of Mercy Critical Care. The office manager, Leslie, seemed more concerned with payment than providing mercy to a life in need. When I brought in a puppy I found, testing positive for Parvo, I was desperate to save its life. Having recently lost two beloved puppies of my own, I knew the agony of watching an innocent life slip away.

I poured my last $200 into the visit and Parvo test, hoping against hope that we could save this little one. The clinic's quote for treatment was $700, a sum that felt insurmountable in that moment. I begged them to call in the prescription so I could use a discount card at the pharmacy, but they refused, demanding full payment upfront.

When I explained my situation, offering to pay the remaining $45 balance later, Leslie's response was cold and unyielding. She wouldn't budge, prioritizing payment over the puppy's life. In that moment, I felt like the clinic's name was a cruel joke. Angel of Mercy? Where was the mercy? Where was the compassion?

As I watched the clock tick away, I couldn't help but wonder if this little puppy's life would be the cost of Leslie's inflexibility. I'm left with a deep sadness, wondering why a clinic would choose a name that seems to mock the very principles of care and compassion that drew them to this profession.

I hope that Angel of Mercy Critical Care will take a long, hard look at their priorities and remember the lives they're sworn to protect. Until then, I'll carry the weight of this experience, and the memory of a puppy left to suffer, with a heavy heart.

staff was very welcoming and kind, they were willing to work around with pricing and took good care of our cat!

I had to bring my beloved 17 year old cat in at around 0100 am today (05/18/2025) to send her to heaven. I wish I had names, but the vet and the assistant were so kind to me at this difficult time. They had an emergency at the same time with another patient, but still managed to give us time and not feel rushed.

My dog couldn't be seen on a Friday afternoon at his normal Vet because they were out of appointments but recommended me taking him to an emergency vet clinic over the weekend so he could get started on antibiotics and get treatment rather than wait until Monday.

I went online where they had an area to make an appointment online. I made one for Saturday and received an email from them showing I made the appointment and to wait for an email from them showing that they accepted the appointment. I should have realized not to come when I did not receive the confirmation email and was told on the phone that I had to come in as a walk-in at 10:45 am, where I had to give all the info I had already done so previously. Over the phone, the receptionist told me there were 2 pets waiting in front of mine, but did not disclose the amount of pets their understaffed techs and vets were already dealing with.

At 12:45pm they told me I was next and would be in the exam room within 30 minutes. We did get into a room by 1:15, but did not see a Tech until 2:55 and the vet just after 3pm.

I understand the traige part and that certain pets with more urgent needs should be taken care of first, but to not have even given my dog an initial check until over 4 hours after coming in is bad practice and I can see where this long of a wait for an initial check can lead to underlying problems with pets that may not show physically.

Fortunately, that was not the case for my dog, and the only reason I'm giving a star is because the Tech and Vet treated my dog great when they finally examined him.
It was my first visit here, and my dog was on the brink of death. Unfortunately, he had to be put down, but the vet staff were so kind and understanding while I was distraught. Thank you all.

I recently had a very disappointing experience at this animal hospital when I took my dog in for help during labor. She had been in labor for over four hours and had only delivered one puppy, and she seemed to be struggling. Initially, it took them two hours to even come up with a solution, and when they finally did, they informed me she had delivered another puppy.

After waiting yet another hour, they suggested an X-ray to check for remaining puppies, which revealed one more. They then recommended keeping her for six more hours and administering medication to help with contractions. The price they quoted me initially went up drastically, and when I asked about alternative options, I was left waiting for nearly 30 minutes for a response that was not forthcoming.

To make matters worse, I found out that the puppies hadn't been fed, and none of them were latching. After the lengthy wait, they gave her the medication and sent us home. They sold me a bottle to feed the pups but provided no milk, rushing us out to find some on our own.

Less than 15 minutes after leaving, my dog passed her third pup, and unfortunately, it was stillborn. I left feeling as though I wasted both time and money at this hospital, as they didn’t seem to take the necessary actions to help us in a timely or compassionate way.

I do not feel that this facility provided the care my dog needed, and I am deeply disappointed in the lack of communication and the overall experience.
